⚠️ Where to Pivot: The presentation views — especially the bottom-right — are so minimal that they reveal how little formal thinking has been committed to. A clean contour line is only powerful when it's describing a deliberate shape; right now it's describing the most generic possible silhouette. The cap is the most underdeveloped element: in all four views it reads as a vague dome with no structural logic about how it attaches, how large it is relative to the body, or what its profile communicates about the product. The shoulder transition (where the body meets the cap) is the most expressive zone of a bottle and it's currently unresolved in every panel.

🛠️ Next Step: Before your next four-panel submission, spend 15 minutes doing a 'shoulder and cap study' — fill one page with 8–10 quick silhouette thumbnails (no construction, just 2-minute gesture outlines) that each propose a different shoulder-to-cap relationship: one with a very abrupt angular shoulder, one with a long gradual taper, one where the cap is disproportionately large, one where the waist pinches dramatically below the shoulder, etc. The goal is not to find the 'right' answer but to force yourself to make a formal decision before you pick up the construction ruler. Bring your chosen silhouette into the next four-panel exercise so that your scaffolding is building toward a specific, chosen form rather than the default.
